title: Digital Innovation for Excellent Patient Care in Hospital
summary: In hospital, people who are confused or disoriented (e.g. due to dementia or delirium) sometimes leave their ward unnoticed and may put themselves at risk. This pilot study tests a technical locating system: participating patients voluntarily wear a small wristband. If a person leaves a defined safe area, the responsible nurse automatically receives a notification on their work phone and can respond quickly. The study examines how reliably the technology works and how nurses experience it in daily practice.
conditions: Wandering/elopement in acute inpatient care as application context. Note: in this pilot, patients are NOT enrolled based on a diagnosis; selection criteria for at-risk patients are explicitly out of scope.

interventions.name: Patients are helping to test the technology by wearing tracking bracelets that send a direct signal to the assigned nurse if the patient leaves the safety zone.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
patients able to consent, non-vulnerable; ≥ 18 years; German-speaking
Exclusion criteria:
patients unable to consent; vulnerable patients; < 18 years
